 Good Question: Why does daylight saving time end so close to Halloween this year? By Victor Puente Published : Oct. 26, 2026 at 5:30 PM EDT | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LEXINGTON, Ky. — For today’s Good Question, Sabrina asks: “Why does daylight saving time end on Halloween night this year? Isn’t it usually in November?”
 Technically, it is in November, just very early in the month.
 What changed in 2005
 The Energy Policy Act of 2005 moved the start of daylight saving time to the second Sunday in March and moved the end to the first Sunday in November.
 Before that, daylight saving time started on the first Sunday in April and ended on the last Sunday in October. The change means daylight saving time is observed for four or five weeks longer, depending on how the calendar falls.
 It also means more trick-or-treating happens in daylight, since the sun sets before 6 p.m. once the clocks fall back.
 Why lawmakers made the shift
 Along with energy savings, lawmakers at the time said child safety was a factor they considered, since fewer kids would be trick-or-treating in the dark.
 When Nov. 1 happens again
 Since the change took effect in 2007, the time change has fallen on Nov. 1 in 2009, 2015, 2020, and this year. The next time it will happen again is in 2037.
